## Trial `zram-swap-ubuntu16__r2Ydqeo`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: a 512MB lz4-compressed zram swap device was created, verified functional under memory pressure, configured with priority 100 (with no competing disk-backed swap present), and confirmed to survive a full, directly-observed reboot cycle (pre-restart baseline, disconnection, reconnection, new boot_id, and recovered service/swap state). ### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Add at least 512MB of compressed in-memory (zram) swap on node1
  - **Why:** swapon --show and /proc/swaps confirm /dev/zram0 at 512M (536870912 bytes) with lz4 compression algorithm selected, and a memory-pressure test (cmd-118bd72f3ed04a35) confirmed the swap is actually usable, driving swap usage to 8.6M under ~900MB allocation on a 999MB-RAM node.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e632a2b1fb894720`, `cmd-2deff6aac1474c56`, `cmd-56a5429255164726`, `cmd-118bd72f3ed04a35`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** zram swap active at boot (persists across reboot)
  - **Why:** zram-swap.service was enabled (symlinked into multi-user.target.wants and swap.target.wants) prior to reboot. A full reboot cycle was captured: pre-restart boot_id and healthy 512M zram swap (cmd-7a9fc9997d644a66), the shutdown command (cmd-9d60ea3c50ad4777), node unreachable twice (cmd-97ae5d9637354088, cmd-c97844af3ba24a8b), reconnection (cmd-380b13c66aff47ff), and post-restart confirmation of a new boot_id plus the service auto-started with 512M lz4 zram swap active at priority 100 (cmd-3332e99b8e1d495f). This matches the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot (75a9f473-7966-4168-a412-144ea086a8ad), corroborating an actual restart occurred.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d74e5f77d8e7401b`, `cmd-7a9fc9997d644a66`, `cmd-9d60ea3c50ad4777`, `cmd-97ae5d9637354088`, `cmd-c97844af3ba24a8b`, `cmd-380b13c66aff47ff`, `cmd-3332e99b8e1d495f`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** zram swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
  - **Why:** The zram device was configured with swap priority 100 (a high value ensuring precedence over typical default-priority disk swap), and /etc/fstab was confirmed to contain no swap entries, meaning no disk-backed swap exists to compete with it. Given the topology has no disk swap at all, the priority setting is sufficient to satisfy the 'preferred over any disk-backed swap' requirement as stated.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e632a2b1fb894720`, `cmd-2deff6aac1474c56`

The verifier assigned hygiene **1.000**. Reviewing all 20 chronological executor commands, every state-changing action has a clear purpose: apt-get update/install (cmd-269f2342673b4086, cmd-21efa610e7c041e3) was a necessary prerequisite to obtain the missing zram kernel module; modprobe zram (cmd-ccc575fc268441ae) and writing the systemd unit plus modules-load.d config (cmd-7f7b0cb9b7094169) directly implement the requirement; the swapoff/rmmod/daemon-reload/enable sequence (cmd-d74e5f77d8e7401b) is a bounded reset to ensure the manually-loaded module state didn't conflict with the new systemd-managed service before enabling it; starting the service (cmd-e632a2b1fb894720) and the reboot (cmd-9d60ea3c50ad4777) are required to configure and verify the outcome. The memory-pressure test (cmd-118bd72f3ed04a35) allocated transient memory that was freed when the Python process exited, leaving no residue. No unnecessary, abandoned, or destructive mutations were found; the after_executor snapshot shows no failed services, no unexpected listening sockets, and no package-health issues, consistent with clean execution.
